claims.text: This measured density of ~859 kg/m³ is significantly lower than what simple ideal (linear) mixing of the pure components would predict. The ethanol–water system is well known for its **negative excess volume**: when ethanol and water are mixed, hydrogen-bonding reorganization causes the mixture to occupy more volume than the sum of the individual pure-liquid volumes. This volume expansion lowers the density below the ideal-mixing estimate.
claims.reason: Negative excess volume signifies contraction and density ABOVE the volume-additive value, not expansion/lower density. The entire causal sign argument is reversed.

evidence.assessment: Negative excess volume signifies contraction and density ABOVE the volume-additive value, not expansion/lower density. The entire causal sign argument is reversed.
